actions.action: Retry only attachments that need attention
actions.mechanism: Track each file independently; a stable receipt makes acceptance durable despite later network errors.
actions.implementation: Show accepted, failed, uploading, or unconfirmed per file. Retry failed files only; reconcile unconfirmed attempts before offering retry. Keep accepted rows unchanged.
actions.check: Accept three files and fail two. Retry must transmit only those two; a later connection error must not reset accepted rows.
actions.risk: Unconfirmed attempts require server reconciliation support; otherwise explain uncertainty instead of silently retrying.

actions.mechanism: Receipt-based recovery preserves accepted attachments while clearly distinguishing unavailable browser-held selections.
actions.implementation: Persist only opaque receipts with a 24-hour expiry. On reopening, validate receipts and fetch display metadata; explain that unfinished uploads require reselection. Never persist file bytes.
actions.check: Close after partial acceptance, then reopen: accepted files remain available without uploading; unfinished selections require reselection. After expiry, no local recovery is promised.
actions.risk: Treat receipts as sensitive bearer references; unavailable validation must not imply missing files.

actions.action: Make reviewed submission a single recoverable commitment
actions.mechanism: An explicit attachment snapshot prevents accidental omissions; server-side idempotency prevents repeated requests from creating duplicate cases.
actions.implementation: Require review of up to five accepted attachments. Invalidate approval after edits. Submit receipt references with a server-issued commitment token; expose completed-case status through associated receipts.
actions.check: Edit after approval: submission requires renewed review. Double-click, lose the response, then reopen within retention: exactly one case exists and its confirmation is recoverable.
actions.risk: Idempotency must identify the reviewed commitment, not globally prohibit legitimate reuse of attachments.
